run1.scope_in: Learning or computing a policy that acts over time in an environment and is judged by long-run return.
run1.scope_out: Predicting a future value without acting on it goes to modality:Temporal Signals; one-shot ranking or recommendation goes to domain:Information Services.
run1.example_children: Reinforcement Learning; Imitation Learning; Model Predictive Control
run1.notes: Largest method branch in the corpus: Reinforcement Learning alone is 263 papers, the 2nd most frequent name. Eight children is justified by that mass.

run1.scope_in: Algorithms that improve a policy or value function from experience: value-based, policy-gradient, actor-critic, offline, distributional, risk-sensitive, constrained.
run1.scope_out: Work on which experience to collect goes to Exploration in Reinforcement Learning; work on where the reward comes from goes to Learning from Human Feedback.
run1.example_children: Proximal Policy Optimization; Offline Reinforcement Learning; Distributional Reinforcement Learning
run1.notes: Absorbs the many '<adjective> Reinforcement Learning' tail names (safe, robust, risk-averse, maximum-entropy, value-based, model-free).

run1.scope_in: How an agent decides what to try: exploration bonuses, intrinsic motivation, option and skill discovery, reset-free data collection.
run1.scope_out: Exploration/exploitation in stateless bandit settings goes to Sequential Decision Processes.
run1.example_children: Intrinsic Motivation; Skill Discovery; Option Discovery
run1.notes: Small but sharply delimited; kept separate because the corpus has a dedicated vocabulary for it (Cooperative Exploration, Exploration Strategies, Optimization of Intrinsic Rewards).

run1.scope_in: Deriving the objective itself from demonstrations, preferences or human judgement rather than from a coded reward.
run1.scope_out: Instruction-tuning a language model with no learned reward model goes to Training Regimes:Transfer Learning; alignment argued as a normative goal goes to concern:AI Safety.
run1.example_children: Imitation Learning; Inverse Reinforcement Learning; Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
run1.notes: Placed under Sequential Decision-Making rather than under Training Regimes because in this corpus every instance is about acquiring a reward or policy for an acting agent.

run1.scope_in: Several learning agents in a shared environment: credit assignment across agents, coordination, centralised-training regimes, emergent communication.
run1.scope_out: Distributing one model’s training across machines goes to Training Regimes:Federated Learning; equilibria analysed rather than learned go to Game-Theoretic Modelling.
run1.example_children: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning; Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE); Language Emergence

run1.scope_in: Equilibria, incentives, mechanism and auction design and welfare objectives, analysed as games.
run1.scope_out: Agents that acquire behaviour by interaction go to Multi-Agent Learning; economics as a field of application goes to domain:Economics.
run1.example_children: Game Theory; Cooperative Game Theory; Coordination Games
run1.notes: Game Theory has 20 papers; it sits here because in this corpus it is almost always about strategic interaction between decision-makers.

run1.scope_in: The decision formalism itself and its properties: MDPs, POMDPs, bandits, partial monitoring, bisimulation.
run1.scope_out: A new algorithm merely evaluated on these formalisms goes to Policy Learning Algorithms.
run1.example_children: Markov Decision Processes; Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes; Contextual Bandits

run1.scope_in: Stability, feedback and optimal control for dynamics that are known or separately identified.
run1.scope_out: Learning the dynamics model itself goes to Dynamical Systems Modelling:System Identification; robot hardware stacks go to domain:Robotics.
run1.example_children: Optimal Control; Control Systems; Lyapunov Stability

run1.scope_in: Search over a model of the world to choose actions: motion and task planning, probabilistic planning, dynamic programming, planning with a learned model.
run1.scope_out: Executing a plan on a physical platform goes to domain:Robotics; planning as an LLM reasoning behaviour goes to modality:Language Model Behaviour.
run1.example_children: Motion Planning; Probabilistic Planning; Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
run1.notes: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning is placed here, not in Policy Learning Algorithms, because its distinguishing act is planning against a learned model. Reviewers may disagree.

run1.scope_in: The design and analysis of algorithms that minimise an objective, and the formulation of decisions as objectives.
run1.scope_out: A statement that a model was 'optimised' for a task carries no method and goes to Not Specified; proofs about learning rather than about an algorithm go to Learning Theory.
run1.example_children: Optimization; Combinatorial Optimization; Stochastic Optimization
run1.notes: Optimization (71 papers) plus a very deep tail of named algorithms; the second-largest method branch.

run1.scope_in: Gradient and proximal methods over continuous variables: stochastic, adaptive, accelerated, distributed, bi-level, minimax, variational-inequality.
run1.scope_out: Methods studied specifically for the behaviour of neural-network training go to Deep Learning Optimization.
run1.example_children: Stochastic Gradient Descent; Stochastic Mirror Descent; First-Order Methods

run1.scope_in: Problems over discrete structures: integer and mixed-integer programming, routing, scheduling, constraint and satisfiability solving, and learned heuristics for them.
run1.scope_out: Continuous relaxations go to Continuous Optimization Algorithms; the industry the instance comes from goes to the domain axis.
run1.example_children: Combinatorial Optimization; Mixed-Integer Linear Programming; Vehicle Routing Problem
run1.notes: Deliberately absorbs the operations-research vocabulary (Operations Research, 19 papers; Personnel Scheduling; Facility Location). I did not create an operations-research domain: OR names get method=Discrete Optimization and, where stated, a domain such as Transportation Systems.

run1.scope_in: Objectives whose data are random or adversarial: stochastic programming, robust and distributionally robust formulations, contextual optimisation.
run1.scope_out: Uncertainty in a model’s predictions goes to concern:Uncertainty Quantification; robustness of a trained model to shifted inputs goes to concern:Robustness to Distribution Shift.
run1.example_children: Stochastic Programming; Robust Optimization; Conditional Robust Optimization

run1.scope_in: Searching a design or configuration space with no usable gradient: Bayesian optimisation, evolutionary search, metaheuristics, architecture and hyper-parameter search.
run1.scope_out: Gradient-based parameter fitting goes to Continuous Optimization Algorithms.
run1.example_children: Bayesian Optimization; Hyper-Parameter Optimization; Neural Architecture Search
run1.notes: Neural Architecture Search is filed here rather than under Neural Architecture Design: its contribution is the search procedure, not the architecture.

run1.scope_in: The empirical behaviour of neural-network training: loss landscapes, training dynamics, implicit regularisation, batch-size and schedule effects, initialisation.
run1.scope_out: Making training cheaper or more parallel goes to concern:Computational Efficiency; bounds on the resulting generalisation go to Learning Theory.
run1.example_children: Training Dynamics; Loss Landscape Analysis; Sharpness-Aware Minimization

run1.scope_in: Building a model of a distribution and computing with it: generative models, posterior inference, graphical structure, sampling.
run1.scope_out: Reporting a predictive uncertainty number as the contribution goes to concern:Uncertainty Quantification; point-estimate predictors go to Classical Machine Learning Methods.
run1.example_children: Generative Models; Bayesian Inference; Variational Inference
run1.notes: Generative Models (83 papers) sits here rather than on an architecture axis: the corpus quotes use it to name a modelling goal, not a network.

run1.scope_in: Neural models of a data distribution and the objectives that train them: diffusion, flows, autoencoding, energy-based, score-based, adversarial, GFlowNets.
run1.scope_out: What is generated (images, molecules, text) is recorded on the modality axis, not here.
run1.example_children: Diffusion Models; Normalizing Flows; Energy-based Models
run1.notes: The single largest concentration of tail names in the corpus after the RL family.

run1.scope_in: Computing or approximating posteriors: variational methods, MCMC, amortised and simulation-based inference, Bayesian deep learning.
run1.scope_out: Bayesian optimisation used as a search strategy goes to Optimization:Black-Box Optimization.
run1.example_children: Variational Inference; Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC); Simulation-Based Inference

run1.scope_in: Models whose contribution is an explicit dependence structure over variables: Bayesian networks, latent-variable and state-space structure, structure learning.
run1.scope_out: Learning on graphs that are themselves the data (citation, molecular, social) goes to modality:Graph-Structured Data.
run1.example_children: Graphical Models; Latent Variable Models; Bayesian Networks
run1.notes: The scope_out line matters: 'graph' in this corpus far more often means the data than the model.

run1.scope_in: Sampling-based simulation of random processes, and the process models behind it.
run1.scope_out: Domain simulators used only as a data source (radiation transport, N-body, crowd) go to the domain axis.
run1.example_children: Monte Carlo Simulations; Stochastic Processes; Temporal Point Processes
run1.notes: Least certain child of this branch; Monte Carlo names in this corpus split between generic sampling and medical-physics dose simulation.

run1.scope_in: How supervision, tasks and data availability are arranged across training — not what is learned, and not with which model.
run1.scope_out: Making training cheaper goes to concern:Computational Efficiency; constructing or cleaning the data goes to Data-Centric Machine Learning; properties of the resulting latent space go to Representation Learning.
run1.example_children: Self-Supervised Learning; Transfer Learning; Continual Learning
run1.notes: Bare Supervised Learning / Classification / Regression names attach to this level directly, with no child.

run1.scope_in: Training on a signal derived from unlabelled data itself: contrastive, predictive and masked pretext objectives, pretraining without labels.
run1.scope_out: What the resulting embedding is like goes to Representation Learning; using someone else’s pretrained model goes to Transfer Learning.
run1.example_children: Contrastive Learning; Self-Supervised Learning (SSL); Language Model Pre-training
run1.notes: Overlaps Representation Learning by construction; the split is signal (here) versus latent structure (there). This is one of my least confident boundaries.

run1.scope_in: Reusing a model trained on one distribution or task for another: fine-tuning, domain adaptation, cross-lingual and sim-to-real transfer, zero- and few-shot use.
run1.scope_out: Generalising to shifted test data with no target-domain training stage goes to concern:Robustness to Distribution Shift; cheap adapters as the contribution go to concern:Efficient Fine-Tuning.
run1.example_children: Domain Adaptation; Sim-to-Real Transfer; Cross-lingual Transfer

run1.scope_in: Learning from a non-stationary stream of tasks without losing what was learned before.
run1.scope_out: Adapting once to a new domain goes to Transfer Learning; detecting that the stream has shifted goes to concern:Robustness to Distribution Shift.
run1.example_children: Catastrophic Forgetting; Class-Incremental Learning; Online Continual Learning

run1.scope_in: Learning a learning procedure, initialisation or parameter generator from a distribution of tasks.
run1.scope_out: Pretrain-then-finetune with no task distribution goes to Transfer Learning.
run1.example_children: Few-Shot Learning; Meta-gradient Learning; Hypernetworks

run1.scope_in: Training one model on several objectives at once, and the interference and weighting problems that creates.
run1.scope_out: One objective over several data types goes to modality:Multimodal Data; sequential rather than simultaneous tasks go to Continual Learning.
run1.example_children: Multi-Task Learning; Multi-Objective Learning; Auxiliary Tasks

run1.scope_in: Training across data holders that never pool their data: aggregation, client heterogeneity, decentralised protocols.
run1.scope_out: Multi-machine training for throughput inside one datacentre goes to concern:Training Scalability; a formal privacy guarantee as the contribution goes to concern:Privacy.
run1.example_children: Federated Learning; Decentralized Learning; Communication-Efficient Learning

run1.scope_in: Training when labels are partial, noisy, indirect or imbalanced.
run1.scope_out: No labels at all goes to Self-Supervised Learning; repairing labels in a released dataset goes to Data-Centric Machine Learning:Data Quality Management.
run1.example_children: Semi-Supervised Learning; Learning with Noisy Labels; Weak Supervision

run1.scope_in: Reaching a target performance from fewer examples by choosing or ordering them: active learning, curriculum, sample-complexity-driven selection.
run1.scope_out: Making each training step cheaper goes to concern:Computational Efficiency; formal sample-complexity results go to Learning Theory.
run1.example_children: Active Learning; Curriculum Learning; Sample Efficiency

run1.scope_in: Predictors and decompositions that do not depend on deep networks: kernels, ensembles, clustering, factorisation, classical regression and estimation.
run1.scope_out: Deep predictors go to Neural Architecture Design or Not Specified; theory about any predictor goes to Learning Theory.
run1.example_children: Support Vector Machines; Gaussian Processes; Ensemble Learning
run1.notes: Kept as a branch because ~60 tail names in this corpus name a pre-deep-learning method, mostly from biomedical and environmental collaborations.

run1.scope_in: Learning through a similarity function: SVMs, Gaussian processes, kernels on structured objects.
run1.scope_out: The Neural Tangent Kernel as an analysis device goes to Learning Theory:Expressivity of Neural Networks.
run1.example_children: Support Vector Machines; Gaussian Processes; Graph Kernels

run1.scope_in: Combining many predictors: bagging, boosting, deep ensembles, model averaging and merging.
run1.scope_out: Ensembles used to produce uncertainty estimates go to concern:Uncertainty Quantification.
run1.example_children: Ensemble Methods; Boosting Algorithms; Model Averaging

run1.scope_in: Finding structure with no target variable: clustering, dimensionality reduction, manifold and spectral methods, matrix and tensor factorisation, ICA.
run1.scope_out: Deep latent-variable models go to Probabilistic Modelling; learned embeddings for downstream use go to Representation Learning:Embedding Methods.
run1.example_children: Clustering; Dimensionality Reduction; Independent Component Analysis (ICA)

run1.scope_in: Estimation and testing in the statistical tradition: regression models, survival analysis, high-dimensional inference, meta-analysis.
run1.scope_out: Causal claims from observational data go to Causal Inference; probabilistic model building goes to Probabilistic Modelling.
run1.example_children: Statistical Inference; Survival Analysis; Generalized Linear Models

run1.scope_in: Work whose object is the training data itself: constructing, augmenting, cleaning, weighting or synthesising it.
run1.scope_out: Datasets built to measure models go to concern:Benchmark Construction; the subject matter of the data goes to the domain axis; formal privacy of the data goes to concern:Privacy.
run1.example_children: Data Augmentation; Synthetic Data; Data Curation

run1.scope_in: Enlarging a training set by transformation or synthesis.
run1.scope_out: Generative modelling studied for its own sake goes to Probabilistic Modelling:Deep Generative Modelling.
run1.example_children: Data Augmentation; Text Data Augmentation; Synthetic Data

run1.scope_in: Detecting and repairing defects in data: missingness, wrong labels, duplicates, inconsistent records.
run1.scope_out: Robustness of a model to noisy labels during training goes to Training Regimes:Weakly Supervised Learning.
run1.example_children: Data Cleaning in Machine Learning; Data Imputation; Label Cleaning

run1.scope_in: Deciding which examples to keep, weight or mine, given a fixed pool.
run1.scope_out: Deciding which examples to label goes to Training Regimes:Data-Efficient Learning.
run1.example_children: Data Valuation; Data Reweighting; Hard Negative Mining
run1.notes: Smallest method child I kept; three data names support it but only just.

run1.scope_in: Estimating or discovering cause-effect relations and the assumptions under which they are identified.
run1.scope_out: Correlational prediction goes to Classical Machine Learning Methods; latent factors without an interventional claim go to Representation Learning.
run1.example_children: Causal Inference; Causal Discovery; CATE Estimation
run1.notes: Only two children, which is the minimum; I did not invent a third.

run1.scope_in: Quantifying the effect of an intervention or treatment from observational or interventional data.
run1.scope_out: Recovering the graph rather than an effect goes to Causal Structure Discovery.
run1.example_children: CATE Estimation; Interventional Data Analysis; Causal Inference in Social Networks

run1.scope_in: Recovering the causal graph or mechanism set from data.
run1.scope_out: Learning on a graph that is given goes to modality:Graph-Structured Data.
run1.example_children: Causal Discovery; Structure Learning; Gene Regulatory Network Inference

run1.scope_in: Work whose object is the structure of the learned latent space: disentanglement, identifiability, object factorisation, geometry, embeddings.
run1.scope_out: The training signal that produced the representation goes to Training Regimes; the network that computes it goes to Neural Architecture Design; the data it represents goes to the modality axis.
run1.example_children: Representation Learning; Disentanglement; Metric Learning
run1.notes: Representation Learning is 56 papers and spawns a large modality-crossed tail (visual, video, graph, protein, audio-text), which is itself evidence for the multi-axis design.

run1.scope_in: Recovering latent factors that vary independently, and the conditions under which they are identifiable.
run1.scope_out: Interventions and effect estimation go to Causal Inference.
run1.example_children: Disentanglement; Identifiable Representation Learning; Nonlinear Independent Component Analysis

run1.scope_in: Learning latents that are claimed to correspond to causal mechanisms or to be identifiable up to a causal equivalence class.
run1.scope_out: Effect estimation on observed variables goes to Causal Inference:Causal Effect Estimation.
run1.example_children: Causal Representation Learning; Causal Feature Learning; Identifiability Theory
run1.notes: A local speciality of this corpus (8 papers on the exact term). In another corpus this would be a leaf of Causal Inference.

run1.scope_in: Decomposing a scene or input into discrete entities or slots.
run1.scope_out: Detecting or segmenting objects with supervision goes to modality:Image Recognition.
run1.example_children: Object-Centric Learning; Object-Centric Representations; Unsupervised Object Discovery

run1.scope_in: Producing vectors whose geometry encodes similarity: metric learning, sparse and discrete codes, embedding spaces for retrieval.
run1.scope_out: Retrieval systems as products go to domain:Search Systems.
run1.example_children: Metric Learning; Text Embeddings; Graph Embedding

run1.scope_in: Formal analysis of learning: generalisation, sample complexity, expressivity, convergence, and measured scaling behaviour.
run1.scope_out: Empirical studies of training behaviour go to Optimization:Deep Learning Optimization; the algorithm being analysed goes to its own method category.
run1.example_children: Machine Learning Theory; Generalization Bounds; Statistical Learning Theory
run1.notes: Empirical Scaling Laws is placed here although it is measured, not proved; it answers the same question about how learning behaves with resources.

run1.scope_in: Bounds and characterisations of the gap between training and test error.
run1.scope_out: Generalisation under a shifted test distribution goes to concern:Robustness to Distribution Shift.
run1.example_children: Generalization Bounds; PAC-Bayesian Theory; Sample Complexity

run1.scope_in: What functions a network family can represent, and the analytic devices used to say so.
run1.scope_out: Designing an architecture to gain a capability goes to Neural Architecture Design.
run1.example_children: Network Expressivity; Neural Tangent Kernel; ReLU Networks

run1.scope_in: Proofs about whether and how fast an iterative learning or optimisation procedure converges.
run1.scope_out: Proposing the algorithm itself goes to Optimization.
run1.example_children: Convergence Analysis; Algorithm Convergence; Stochastic Convex Optimization

run1.scope_in: Measured relationships between model size, data, compute and performance.
run1.scope_out: Engineering that makes large-scale training feasible goes to concern:Training Scalability.
run1.example_children: Scaling Laws; Deep Learning Scaling Laws; Language Model Scaling

run1.scope_in: Work whose contribution is an architectural component or inductive bias in its own right.
run1.scope_out: A name that only states the backbone used (Transformers, Convolutional Neural Networks, Graph Neural Networks, Autoencoders) is not a research topic here: it goes to Not Specified on this axis and is recorded on the modality axis instead. Automatic search over architectures goes to Optimization:Black-Box Optimization; shrinking an architecture goes to concern:Model Compression.
run1.example_children: Equivariant Neural Networks; Mixture of Experts; Neuromorphic Computing
run1.notes: This is my answer to the architecture question: architectures are not a research area in this survey, but architecture DESIGN is. 28 backbone-only names cover 161 paper-mentions (2.7%); 76 of those are Graph Neural Networks, which the modality axis captures as graph data, leaving ~1.4% of mentions in the Not Specified bucket to be excluded in favour of the project’s separate architecture ontology.

run1.scope_in: Architectures built around a symmetry or geometric structure of the input.
run1.scope_out: The geometry of the learned latent space goes to Representation Learning.
run1.example_children: Equivariant Neural Networks; Geometric Deep Learning; Equivariance in Neural Networks

run1.scope_in: Architectures that route inputs to a subset of parameters: mixtures of experts, gating, modularity, dynamic depth or width.
run1.scope_out: Static sparsification for speed goes to concern:Model Compression.
run1.example_children: Mixture of Experts; Modular Neural Networks; Gating Mechanisms

run1.scope_in: Architectures and hardware whose design argument is a biological mechanism.
run1.scope_out: Using networks to model measured neural data goes to domain:Computational Neuroscience.
run1.example_children: Neuromorphic Computing; Reservoir Computing; Neuroscience-inspired AI
run1.notes: Smallest branch of this parent; retained because its three names are unplaceable elsewhere.

run1.scope_in: Learning, emulating or solving the time evolution of a physical or mechanistic system.
run1.scope_out: Forecasting an observed series with no mechanistic model goes to modality:Time Series Forecasting; controlling a system whose dynamics are given goes to Sequential Decision-Making:Control Theory.
run1.example_children: Dynamical Systems; Physics-Informed Neural Networks; Neural Differential Equations
run1.notes: Small (~25 names) but unmergeable: it is the only method family whose object is a differential equation rather than a dataset.

run1.scope_in: Networks that solve or approximate solution operators of differential equations.
run1.scope_out: Numerical analysis with no learned component goes to domain:Physical Sciences.
run1.example_children: Neural Operators; Partial Differential Equation Solvers; Physics-Informed Neural Networks

run1.scope_in: Learned fast approximations of an expensive simulator.
run1.scope_out: Inference about simulator parameters goes to Probabilistic Modelling:Bayesian Inference.
run1.example_children: Surrogate Modeling; Climate Model Emulation; Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs)

run1.scope_in: Recovering the governing dynamics or operator of a system from observed trajectories.
run1.scope_out: Recovering a causal graph over variables goes to Causal Inference:Causal Structure Discovery.
run1.example_children: System Identification; Koopman Operators; Inverse Dynamics Modeling

run1.scope_in: Names that state no technical method: bare umbrellas (Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Artificial Intelligence), pure application or field names, and backbone-only architecture names.
run1.scope_out: Anything naming a family of algorithms, objectives or analyses belongs in one of the eleven method categories, however briefly it is stated.
run1.example_children: Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Transformer Networks
run1.notes: Residual bucket, measured: 40 contentless umbrella names account for 517 of 5990 paper-mentions (8.6%); backbone-only names add ~1.4%. Names filed here are usually informative on another axis, so they are not lost.

run1.scope_in: Work on text, on linguistic structure, or on the behaviour of models of text.
run1.scope_out: Source code goes to Source Code; spoken audio goes to Acoustic Signals; text paired with images goes to Multimodal Data.
run1.example_children: Natural Language Processing; Language Modeling; Machine Translation
run1.notes: Natural Language Processing is the single most frequent name in the corpus (295 papers).

run1.scope_in: Tasks whose output is a label, span, structure or answer derived from given text.
run1.scope_out: Producing new text goes to Language Generation; ranking documents for a user goes to domain:Search Systems.
run1.example_children: Question Answering; Natural Language Inference; Named Entity Recognition

run1.scope_in: Tasks whose output is text: translation, summarisation, dialogue, controlled and conditional generation.
run1.scope_out: Generic generative-model methodology goes to method:Deep Generative Modelling.
run1.example_children: Text Generation; Text Summarization; Dialogue Systems

run1.scope_in: Language studied as an object: syntax, semantics, pragmatics, sociolinguistics, grammar.
run1.scope_out: Engineering a parser to improve a downstream task goes to Language Understanding.
run1.example_children: Syntax; Dependency Parsing; Lexical Semantics

run1.scope_in: Work whose difficulty is the number of languages or the scarcity of data in them.
run1.scope_out: Transfer machinery studied independently of language goes to method:Transfer Learning.
run1.example_children: Multilingual NLP; Low-Resource Languages; Multilingual Models

run1.scope_in: Study and steering of large pretrained language models as objects: prompting, in-context learning, reasoning traces, retrieval augmentation, factual recall.
run1.scope_out: Opening the model to explain its computation goes to concern:Mechanistic Interpretability; efficiency of serving it goes to concern:Computational Efficiency.
run1.example_children: Large Language Models; In-Context Learning; Prompt Engineering
run1.notes: A modality child rather than a method: in this corpus these names always presuppose text, and their claims are about a text model’s behaviour.

run1.scope_in: Work on images, video, or 3D visual structure.
run1.scope_out: Images of molecules or graphs drawn as pictures are rare here; molecular and graph data go to their own categories. Rendering as an end product goes to domain:Computer Graphics.
run1.example_children: Computer Vision; Image Classification; Semantic Segmentation
run1.notes: Computer Vision is 240 papers, the 4th most frequent name. Six children, justified by the size and breadth of the visual tail.

run1.scope_in: Assigning labels, boxes or masks to the content of an image.
run1.scope_out: Detecting that an image is out of distribution goes to concern:Out-of-Distribution Detection; medical images go to Biomedical Imaging.
run1.example_children: Image Classification; Object Detection; Semantic Segmentation

run1.scope_in: Producing or editing image content.
run1.scope_out: Text-conditioned image generation goes to Multimodal Data:Text-to-Image Generation; the generative machinery itself goes to method:Deep Generative Modelling.
run1.example_children: Image Generation; Image-to-Image Translation; Image Editing

run1.scope_in: Work whose difficulty is the temporal dimension of visual data.
run1.scope_out: Non-visual time series go to Temporal Signals.
run1.example_children: Video Prediction; Object Tracking; Activity Recognition

run1.scope_in: Representing, reconstructing or rendering three-dimensional geometry: meshes, point clouds, radiance fields, depth, SLAM mapping.
run1.scope_out: 3D molecular geometry goes to Biomolecular Data; robot navigation using a map goes to domain:Robot Navigation.
run1.example_children: 3D Reconstruction; Neural Radiance Fields; Point Cloud Processing

run1.scope_in: Images acquired from living systems and the pipelines specific to them: MRI, CT, PET, ultrasound, microscopy, histology, radiomics.
run1.scope_out: The clinical question the image answers goes to domain:Health; brain-mapping analyses go to domain:Human Brain Mapping.
run1.example_children: Medical Imaging; Neuroimaging; Microscopy
run1.notes: Roughly 60 names, the densest single cluster in the corpus tail. Splitting it across Image Recognition and domain:Health would have destroyed it.

run1.scope_in: Operations on the image signal itself: registration, reconstruction, deconvolution, compression, denoising.
run1.scope_out: Semantic content extraction goes to Image Recognition.
run1.example_children: Image Registration; Image Compression; Image Deconvolution

run1.scope_in: Work on sound: speech, music, and environmental or biological audio.
run1.scope_out: Text transcripts analysed without audio go to Natural Language; general one-dimensional signals go to Temporal Signals.
run1.example_children: Speech Recognition; Speech Processing; Audio Classification

run1.scope_in: Mapping speech audio to text or to speaker-independent linguistic labels.
run1.scope_out: Producing speech goes to Speech Synthesis; identifying who is speaking goes to Speaker Modelling.
run1.example_children: Automatic Speech Recognition; Speech-to-Text Translation; Accent Classification

run1.scope_in: Producing or modifying speech audio: text-to-speech, enhancement, separation, voice editing.
run1.scope_out: Generative-model methodology goes to method:Deep Generative Modelling.
run1.example_children: Text-to-Speech (TTS); Speech Enhancement; Speech Separation

run1.scope_in: Characterising the speaker rather than the content: verification, embeddings, paralinguistics.
run1.scope_out: Emotion inferred from text goes to Natural Language:Language Understanding.
run1.example_children: Speaker Verification; Speaker Embedding; Speech Emotion Recognition

run1.scope_in: Audio work whose object is music.
run1.scope_out: Recommending music to users goes to domain:Recommender Systems.
run1.example_children: Music Generation; Music Source Separation; Music Information Retrieval (MIR)

run1.scope_in: Work whose data are nodes and edges: molecular, citation, social, biological, knowledge and temporal graphs.
run1.scope_out: Graphs used as a probabilistic model of dependence go to method:Probabilistic Graphical Models; molecules treated chemically rather than as graphs go to Biomolecular Data.
run1.example_children: Graph Neural Networks; Graph Learning; Node Classification
run1.notes: Graph Neural Networks (76 papers) is recorded here rather than as an architecture: the name reliably tells you the data are graphs, which is exactly what this axis measures.

run1.scope_in: Predicting attributes of individual nodes.
run1.scope_out: Predicting a property of the whole graph goes to Graph-Level Prediction.
run1.example_children: Node Classification; Semi-Supervised Node Classification; Graph Anomaly Detection (GAD)

run1.scope_in: Predicting the existence or evolution of edges.
run1.scope_out: Reasoning over typed relations in a knowledge base goes to Knowledge Graphs.
run1.example_children: Link Prediction; Dynamic Link Prediction; Graph Recovery

run1.scope_in: Predicting a property of an entire graph, and comparing graphs.
run1.scope_out: Molecular property prediction, where the chemistry is the point, goes to Biomolecular Data.
run1.example_children: Graph Classification; Graph Regression; Graph Kernels

run1.scope_in: Graphs whose structure changes over time.
run1.scope_out: Static graphs with time-varying node features only go to Node-Level Prediction.
run1.example_children: Temporal Graph Learning; Dynamic Graphs; Temporal Network Models

run1.scope_in: Typed, symbolic relational stores and reasoning over them, including ontologies and taxonomies.

run1.scope_in: Work on making a model’s computation or decision legible to a person.

run1.scope_in: Reverse-engineering internal computation: circuits, probes, representations, visualisation of units.

run1.scope_in: Work on reducing the compute, memory, energy or latency a model needs.

run1.example_children: Model Compression; Efficient Deep Learning; Efficient Inference
run1.notes: This is where the architecture-shrinking vocabulary goes (pruning, quantisation, distillation). Reading it as a concern rather than as architecture work is deliberate: the papers are about a budget, not about a design.

run1.scope_in: Making a trained model smaller or cheaper to run: distillation, quantisation, pruning, sparsification.
run1.scope_out: Sparsity as an architectural routing mechanism goes to method:Conditional Computation.
run1.example_children: Knowledge Distillation; Model Quantization; Network Pruning

run1.scope_in: Adapting a large pretrained model while updating few parameters.
run1.scope_out: Whether the adaptation transfers at all goes to method:Transfer Learning.

run1.scope_in: Making large-scale training feasible: parallelism, memory, communication, throughput.

run1.example_children: Distributed Training; Model Parallelism; Large Batch Training

run1.scope_in: Work whose contribution is how we measure models rather than the models themselves.
run1.scope_out: Reporting a metric while proposing a method is not evaluation work; a dataset built to train rather than to test goes to method:Data-Centric Machine Learning.

run1.scope_in: Building the tasks and datasets against which models are compared.
run1.scope_out: Augmenting or cleaning training data goes to method:Data-Centric Machine Learning.

run1.scope_in: Designing and validating the measures themselves.
run1.scope_out: Calibration of predicted probabilities goes to Uncertainty Quantification.
run1.example_children: Evaluation Metrics; Metric Evaluation; Evaluation Metrics for Natural Language Generation

run1.scope_in: How experiments are designed, reported and reproduced.
run1.scope_out: Statistical estimation as a method goes to method:Classical Statistical Inference.
run1.example_children: Empirical Study; Reproducibility in Medical Imaging; Experimental Design

run1.scope_in: Work on the normative and institutional questions raised by AI systems: ethics, regulation, safety and societal effect.

run1.example_children: AI Ethics; AI Governance; Responsible AI

run1.scope_in: Normative analysis of what AI systems ought to do and to whom.
run1.scope_out: Research-ethics procedure for human subjects goes to domain:Health.
run1.example_children: AI Ethics; Ethical AI; Neuroethics

run1.scope_in: Rules, oversight, auditing and transparency obligations for AI systems.
run1.scope_out: Auditing a specific model for bias goes to Bias Measurement.
run1.example_children: AI Policy; AI Regulation; Algorithmic Transparency

run1.scope_in: Preventing capable systems from pursuing unintended objectives, including alignment and misgeneralisation of goals.

run1.scope_in: Effects of AI deployment on communities, labour, equity and the environment, studied as such.
run1.scope_out: A specific fairness metric goes to Fairness; environmental cost measured in compute goes to Computational Efficiency.
run1.example_children: Societal Impacts and Adaptation; Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) in AI; Science and Technology Studies

run1.scope_in: Names that raise no cross-cutting concern about the system, which is most of the corpus.
run1.scope_out: A name that states a property of the model as the point (fair, private, robust, explainable, efficient, evaluated) takes that concern.
run1.example_children: Reinforcement Learning; Genomics; Image Classification
run1.notes: Expected to be the value for roughly four names in five. That is the measurement this axis exists to make.

run2.scope_in: Names that assert only that the work is machine learning, deep learning or AI, and identify no sub-area, task, method or subject matter.
run2.scope_out: A name that adds any qualifier with content ('Machine Learning for Genomics', 'Deep Learning Theory', 'Machine Learning Security') is not an umbrella label and goes to the branch named by the qualifier.
run2.example_children: Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Artificial Intelligence
run2.notes: 8.4% of paper-mentions (501/5990) land here, concentrated in 'Machine Learning' (249) and 'Deep Learning' (177). These are the two most frequent names in the corpus and they carry no information. Quarantining them is the single most important hygiene decision in this proposal: dumping them into any substantive branch would make that branch the largest in the report for no reason. Report this branch as a line, then exclude it from the area shares.

run2.scope_in: Bare 'machine learning' labels and their trivial variants, including generic 'applied/methods-driven ML' phrasings.
run2.scope_out: 'Machine Learning Theory' -> Learning Theory; 'Machine Learning Security' -> Adversarial Robustness; 'Machine Learning for X' -> the branch for X.
run2.example_children: Machine Learning; Machine Learning Algorithms; Machine Learning Applications
run2.notes: 249 papers on the bare name alone.

run2.scope_in: Bare 'deep learning' and bare 'neural network' labels that name no architecture family, training question or application.
run2.scope_out: 'Deep Learning Theory' -> Learning Theory; 'Recurrent Neural Networks', 'Transformers' -> Neural Architecture Design; 'Deep Reinforcement Learning' -> Reinforcement Learning.
run2.example_children: Deep Learning; Neural Networks; Artificial Neural Networks
run2.notes: 177 + 19 + 4 papers. The boundary with Neural Architecture Design is the presence of a named family.

run2.scope_in: Bare 'artificial intelligence' labels, including AGI and 'intelligent systems' used as a field name.
run2.scope_out: 'AI Safety', 'AI Ethics', 'Explainable AI' all have content and go to Trustworthy Machine Learning.
run2.example_children: Artificial Intelligence; Artificial General Intelligence; Intelligent Systems
run2.notes: Small (~18 papers) but must not be merged into General Machine Learning: some reports will want AI-as-a-field separated.

run2.scope_in: Names that describe the shape of a piece of research rather than its subject: 'Algorithms', 'Theory', 'Empirical Study', 'Interdisciplinary Studies', 'Data Analysis'.
run2.scope_out: 'Algorithm Convergence' -> Optimization Algorithms; 'Evaluation Methods' -> Evaluation Methodology; 'Theoretical Neuroscience' -> Neuroscience.
run2.example_children: Algorithms; Interdisciplinary Studies; Empirical Study
run2.notes: This is the proposal's only residual bucket. It holds ~25 paper-mentions (<0.5%). If an annotator is tempted to use it for anything else, the name belongs somewhere real.

run2.scope_in: Research areas defined by how the learning problem itself is set up: what experience the learner receives, what it must produce, and across what it must generalize.
run2.scope_out: Areas defined by the kind of data (text, images, graphs) -> Data-Modality Subfields; areas defined by a property the trained model must have (fair, private, robust) -> Trustworthy Machine Learning; the mathematics of the algorithm -> Formal Foundations of Machine Learning.
run2.example_children: Reinforcement Learning; Self-Supervised Learning; Transfer Learning
run2.notes: Largest ML branch in the corpus, driven by Reinforcement Learning (263). 10 children is at the rule-6 limit; each is a name the corpus uses hundreds or dozens of times and none subsumes another.

run2.scope_in: Learning a policy from interaction with an environment that has state and transitions, including its variants, its algorithmic families, and its credit-assignment and exploration questions.
run2.scope_out: Bandit problems with no state transitions -> Online Learning; control of a known dynamical system -> Control Theory; RL used as a tool on a robot -> Robotics if the name says 'robot', here if the name says 'RL'.
run2.example_children: Deep Reinforcement Learning; Offline Reinforcement Learning; Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
run2.notes: 263 papers on the bare name, plus ~120 distinct RL sub-names in the tail (option discovery, credit assignment, replay buffers, MDPs/POMDPs, policy gradients). By far the largest single research area in this corpus.

run2.scope_in: Learning from labelled examples, and research on the supply and quality of those labels: semi-supervised, weak, active, noisy-label and class-imbalanced settings.
run2.scope_out: Self-supervised pretext tasks -> Self-Supervised Learning; 'Image Classification' -> Computer Vision (the name commits to a modality, not to a supervision regime).
run2.example_children: Semi-Supervised Learning; Active Learning; Learning with Noisy Labels
run2.notes: The bare names ('Supervised Learning' 10, 'Classification' 5, 'Regression' 2) are thin; the category is carried by the label-efficiency tail.

run2.scope_in: Learning from a signal constructed out of unlabelled data itself, including contrastive and non-contrastive objectives and masked prediction.
run2.scope_out: What the learned features are for or what structure they should have -> Representation Learning; using a pretrained model on a new task -> Transfer Learning.
run2.example_children: Contrastive Learning; Contrastive and Non-Contrastive Learning; Self-Supervised Learning (Graph Data)
run2.notes: 73 + 21 papers. Kept separate from Representation Learning on purpose: SSL names a training signal, Representation Learning names a property of the output. Annotators will confuse them; the scope_out lines are load-bearing.

run2.scope_in: Research on what a learned latent space should contain and how it is structured: disentanglement, identifiability, invariance, metric structure, dimensionality.
run2.scope_out: The objective used to obtain it -> Self-Supervised Learning; a representation of a specific data type ('Graph Representation Learning', 'Protein Representation Learning') -> the modality or domain branch.
run2.example_children: Disentanglement; Causal Representation Learning; Metric Learning
run2.notes: 56 papers plus a large tail (manifold learning, object-centric representations, discrete representations, identifiability).

run2.scope_in: Learning a distribution in order to sample from it, and the model families defined by how they do so.
run2.scope_out: Generation of a specific medium named in the label ('Image Generation', 'Text-to-Image Synthesis', 'Molecule Generation') -> the modality or domain branch; likelihood-based inference without a sampler -> Probabilistic Inference.
run2.example_children: Diffusion Models; Normalizing Flows; Generative Adversarial Networks
run2.notes: 'Generative Models' (83) is the 7th most frequent name. This is the clearest case of an architecture word used as the name of a research problem; see the architecture policy in RATIONALE.md.

run2.scope_in: Reusing or sharing what was learned on one task, domain, language or environment in another, including few-shot, zero-shot, domain adaptation, multi-task and meta-learning.
run2.scope_out: Keeping old tasks while learning new ones over time -> Continual Learning; measuring degradation under a shift you did not choose -> Distribution-Shift Robustness.
run2.example_children: Domain Adaptation; Few-Shot Learning; Meta-Learning
run2.notes: Meta-Learning (26 papers) is folded in rather than made a sibling: the corpus contains only two other meta-* names, so a separate category would fail the three-example test. This is one of my least-certain calls.

run2.scope_in: Learning a sequence of tasks over time without losing what was learned earlier.
run2.scope_out: Transferring to one new task and stopping -> Transfer Learning; learning from a data stream with a regret objective -> Online Learning; deliberately removing knowledge -> Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning.
run2.example_children: Catastrophic Forgetting; Lifelong Learning; Class-Incremental Learning
run2.notes: 29 papers plus ~12 tail names. Boundary with Online Learning is task sequence vs sample stream.

run2.scope_in: Training one model across parties that do not pool their data, and the communication, heterogeneity and aggregation problems that follow.
run2.scope_out: Data-parallel training inside one cluster -> Machine Learning Systems Engineering; the privacy guarantee itself -> Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning.
run2.example_children: Decentralized Learning; Communication-Efficient Learning; Byzantine Robustness
run2.notes: 24 papers. Deliberately not merged with distributed training: the corpus treats them as different literatures.

run2.scope_in: Deciding whether an input is unlike the training distribution or unlike normal operation, as the task being solved.
run2.scope_out: Making a model perform well under shift rather than flagging it -> Distribution-Shift Robustness; detecting adversarially crafted inputs -> Adversarial Robustness.
run2.example_children: Out-of-Distribution Detection; Outlier Detection; Time-Series Anomaly Detection
run2.notes: 20 + 12 papers plus a tail (log-based, graph, fraud, misclassification detection). The near-homonym pair 'OOD Detection' (here) / 'OOD Generalization' (Trustworthy) is the highest-risk confusion in the whole structure.

run2.scope_in: Learning from a stream of data or decisions under a regret or exploration objective, without a fixed training set.
run2.scope_out: Interaction with a stateful environment -> Reinforcement Learning; convergence analysis of a batch optimizer -> Optimization Algorithms.
run2.example_children: Multi-armed Bandits; Contextual Bandits; Online Convex Optimization
run2.notes: Small (~15 paper-mentions) and added after the tail sample: 'Dynamic Learning', 'Concept Drift', 'Performative Prediction', 'Streaming SGD' had no home without it.

run2.scope_in: The classical subfields of machine learning, each individuated by the kind of data it works on rather than by the method it uses or the science it serves.
run2.scope_out: The scientific or professional subject that supplies the data ('Medical Imaging', 'Neuroimaging', 'Remote Sensing') -> the domain branch; the learning setup used ('Self-Supervised Learning') -> Learning Problem Formulations.
run2.example_children: Natural Language Processing; Computer Vision; Graph Machine Learning
run2.notes: Holds the two largest names in the corpus (NLP 295, CV 240). The head rule matters here: a name that pairs a modality with a science ('Medical Image Segmentation') is filed under the science, because the survey is being read by an institute that wants to know how much clinical work it does.

run2.scope_in: Machine learning over human language in text form: tasks, language models, multilinguality, and the linguistic behaviour of text models.
run2.scope_out: Language as an object of linguistic study -> Linguistics; generating or analysing source code -> Software Engineering; modality-agnostic adaptation techniques (prompting, PEFT) -> Foundation Model Adaptation.
run2.example_children: Machine Translation; Question Answering; Text Summarization
run2.notes: 295 papers, the single most frequent name. LLM-specific names (language modeling, instruction tuning, RAG, chain-of-thought) sit here at depth 3 except where the technique is modality-agnostic.

run2.scope_in: Machine learning over images, video, 3D geometry and rendered scenes.
run2.scope_out: Images of a body or a specimen -> Medical Imaging; satellite and aerial imagery -> Environmental Monitoring; vision on a robot -> Robotics if the name says robot.
run2.example_children: Image Classification; Object Detection; Semantic Segmentation
run2.notes: 240 papers plus a very large tail (3D reconstruction, NeRF, rendering, video, image generation, point clouds). Computer Graphics (9) is included here; the corpus never separates them.

run2.scope_in: Machine learning over acoustic signals of any kind: speech, music, environmental and bioacoustic sound.
run2.scope_out: The linguistic content once transcribed -> Natural Language Processing; EEG/MEG and other biosignals -> Neuroscience.
run2.example_children: Speech Recognition; Speech Enhancement; Music Information Retrieval (MIR)
run2.notes: ~45 paper-mentions. Named 'Audio Processing' rather than 'Speech and Audio' to keep one concept per category; scope_in states explicitly that speech belongs here, because annotators will not assume it.

run2.scope_in: Learning on data whose primary structure is a graph: node, edge and graph-level tasks, message passing, graph expressivity, dynamic and heterophilic graphs.
run2.scope_out: Graphs as a combinatorial optimization instance (routing, TSP, SAT) -> Combinatorial Optimization; molecular graphs where the name says molecule -> Drug Discovery or Computational Chemistry.
run2.example_children: Graph Neural Networks; Node Classification; Link Prediction
run2.notes: 'Graph Neural Networks' (76) is classified here, not as an architecture: in this corpus it is used as the name of the field. Includes Graph Theory (6) and Spectral Graph Theory where used to analyse learning.

run2.scope_in: Learning over ordered signals indexed by time: forecasting, temporal point processes, change points, sequence models over non-linguistic series.
run2.scope_out: Detection framed as the task -> Anomaly Detection; a time series of brain, climate or market data where the name says so -> the domain branch.
run2.example_children: Time Series Forecasting; Temporal Point Processes; Sequence Modeling
run2.notes: ~30 paper-mentions. 'Sequence Modeling' (8) is placed here rather than in NLP; that is a judgement call and the quotes are split.

run2.scope_in: Learning that must align or fuse two or more modalities, and the models and benchmarks defined by that pairing.
run2.scope_out: A single modality with an auxiliary signal -> that modality; multi-omics data fusion -> Computational Biology.
run2.example_children: Vision-Language Models; Visual Question Answering; Audio-Text Representation Learning
run2.notes: 15 + 11 + 4 papers plus a tail. Vision-language dominates; audio-text and vision-touch exist but are rare.

run2.scope_in: Finding, ranking or recommending items that satisfy a user's information need, over document, product, media or interaction data.
run2.scope_out: Understanding a query's meaning as a language problem -> Natural Language Processing; the interface through which results are presented -> Human-Computer Interaction.
run2.example_children: Recommender Systems; Learning to Rank; Entity Matching
run2.notes: 19 + 16 papers. Weakest fit in this branch: its 'modality' is really a task shape. I keep it here rather than inventing a one-member branch, and flag it in RATIONALE.md.

run2.scope_in: Research on how to build, train, adapt and shrink neural networks, stated independently of the data they are applied to.
run2.scope_out: Why deep networks generalize, as mathematics -> Learning Theory; architectures specialised to one modality ('Vision Transformers') -> that modality; the hardware and pipelines that run training -> Machine Learning Systems Engineering.
run2.example_children: Attention Mechanisms; Knowledge Distillation; Prompt Engineering
run2.notes: Four children only, and that is honest: the corpus has a lot of deep-learning practice vocabulary but it clusters tightly into these four.

run2.scope_in: Research about the architectural components and design principles of neural networks: attention, memory, modularity, equivariance by construction, architecture search.
run2.scope_out: A family used as the name of a research area (Graph Neural Networks, Diffusion Models) -> its field; making an existing architecture smaller or faster -> Model Compression.
run2.example_children: Attention Mechanisms; Neural Architecture Search; Mixture of Experts
run2.notes: ~50 paper-mentions. This is the only category that is genuinely about architectures-as-architectures and therefore the only one that overlaps the project's separate architecture ontology. Report it flagged.

run2.scope_in: The empirical business of getting a network to train: optimizers in practice, learning-rate and batch-size choices, initialization, regularization, training dynamics, scaling behaviour.
run2.scope_out: Convergence proofs and rates -> Optimization Algorithms; generalization bounds -> Learning Theory.
run2.example_children: Neural Network Optimization; Training Dynamics; Regularization Techniques
run2.notes: Its boundary with Optimization Algorithms is the proposal's second-riskiest seam: 'practice vs proof'. Stated as: if the name mentions a network or a training run, it lands here.

run2.scope_in: Reducing a trained model's size, latency or energy while keeping its behaviour: distillation, pruning, quantization, sparsity, efficient inference.
run2.scope_out: Distributing training over machines -> Machine Learning Systems Engineering; environmental cost arguments -> Responsible AI.
run2.example_children: Knowledge Distillation; Neural Network Pruning; Quantization
run2.notes: ~45 paper-mentions across a dozen near-synonyms ('Model Compression', 'Network Compression', 'Efficient Deep Learning', 'Model Efficiency').

run2.scope_in: Steering an already-pretrained large model without retraining it from scratch: prompting, in-context learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, instruction tuning, preference tuning, model merging.
run2.scope_out: Transfer between small task-specific models -> Transfer Learning; what the adapted model should be safe or aligned with -> AI Safety.
run2.example_children: Prompt Engineering; In-Context Learning; Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)
run2.notes: A 2024 cluster that did not exist in earlier corpora; ~35 paper-mentions, almost all in the one-paper tail. Placing RLHF here rather than under Reinforcement Learning is deliberate and arguable.

run2.scope_in: The mathematics that learning algorithms are built out of and analysed with: optimization, probability, causality, geometry, strategic interaction, dynamics.
run2.scope_out: Empirical recipes for training networks -> Deep Learning Methodology; the same mathematics applied to a named science ('Molecular Dynamics') -> that science.
run2.example_children: Optimization Algorithms; Probabilistic Inference; Causal Inference
run2.notes: Nine children. This branch is where an institute's theory strength shows up; 'Optimization' alone is 71 papers and 'Bayesian Inference' 19.

run2.scope_in: Continuous optimization as an object of study: convexity, stochastic and first-order methods, convergence rates, variance reduction, distributed and bilevel formulations.
run2.scope_out: Discrete or integer decision problems -> Combinatorial Optimization; tuning a training run -> Neural Network Training; hyperparameter search as a service -> Evaluation Methodology.
run2.example_children: Convex Optimization; Stochastic Optimization; First-Order Methods
run2.notes: 'Optimization' (71) is the 10th most frequent name and its quotes are overwhelmingly continuous-optimization. ~60 further tail names (mirror descent, Polyak stepsize, variational inequalities, minimax).

run2.scope_in: Discrete decision problems and the algorithms that solve them: integer programming, routing, scheduling, constraint programming, and learned heuristics for them.
run2.scope_out: The industry that poses the problem ('Public Transport', 'Personnel Scheduling' as a workforce topic) -> Transportation Systems or Industrial Engineering; continuous relaxations studied for their own sake -> Optimization Algorithms.
run2.example_children: Mixed Integer Programming; Vehicle Routing Problem; Job-Shop Scheduling
run2.notes: 17 papers on the bare name plus 'Operations Research' (19) and ~40 tail names. Also the home for decision-focused / predict-then-optimize names such as 'Contextual Optimization' and 'Prescriptive Analytics'.

run2.scope_in: Formal statements about what can be learned and how well: generalization bounds, sample complexity, expressivity, identifiability, and the theory of deep networks.
run2.scope_out: Measured generalization gaps in experiments -> Neural Network Training; guarantees about a specific trained network -> Neural Network Verification.
run2.example_children: Generalization Bounds; PAC-Bayesian Theory; Statistical Learning Theory
run2.notes: Includes 'Machine Learning Theory' (8), 'Deep Learning Theory' (7), 'Theoretical Machine Learning' (5) and information-theoretic names; ~45 paper-mentions.

run2.scope_in: Computing or approximating posteriors and likelihoods: Bayesian inference, variational methods, Monte Carlo, graphical models, density estimation, simulation-based inference.
run2.scope_out: Learning a sampler as the research goal -> Generative Modeling; predicting a calibrated confidence for a downstream decision -> Uncertainty Quantification.
run2.example_children: Bayesian Inference; Variational Inference; Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)
run2.notes: 19 papers on 'Bayesian Inference' plus ~50 tail names. The seam with Generative Modeling is real (normalizing flows appear in both literatures); the rule is whether the name is about inference or about sampling.

run2.scope_in: Reasoning about interventions and counterfactuals: causal discovery, treatment-effect estimation, structure identifiability, causal representations.
run2.scope_out: Correlational prediction in an applied field -> that field; epidemiological study design -> Public Health.
run2.example_children: Causal Discovery; Causal Representation Learning; CATE Estimation
run2.notes: 16 + 8 + 6 papers plus ~20 tail names. A distinct and visible cluster in this corpus, not a sub-branch of statistics.

run2.scope_in: Strategic interaction between multiple decision makers: equilibria, cooperative and non-cooperative games, mechanism design, multi-agent systems as a formalism.
run2.scope_out: Multi-agent reinforcement learning as a training method -> Reinforcement Learning; auctions as an economic subject -> Economics.
run2.example_children: Multi-Agent Systems; Cooperative Game Theory; Coordination Games
run2.notes: 20 + 11 papers. Placed under foundations rather than with RL because its quotes are about equilibrium analysis, not about learning algorithms.

run2.scope_in: Geometric and topological structure used as a modelling principle: symmetry and equivariance, manifolds, optimal transport, spectral and kernel geometry.
run2.scope_out: An equivariant architecture named as an architecture -> Neural Architecture Design; 3D scene geometry -> Computer Vision.
run2.example_children: Geometric Deep Learning; Optimal Transport; Manifold Learning
run2.notes: 11 + 8 + 4 papers plus ~25 tail names (scattering transforms, statistical manifolds, Lorentz invariance in a learning sense, equivariance).

run2.scope_in: Driving a dynamical system to a desired behaviour with stability guarantees, and identifying such systems: optimal control, MPC, Lyapunov analysis, system identification.
run2.scope_out: Learning a controller by trial and error -> Reinforcement Learning; the robot or grid being controlled -> Robotics or Energy Systems.
run2.example_children: Model Predictive Control; Optimal Control; Dynamical Systems
run2.notes: ~40 paper-mentions. Sits under foundations because the corpus names it as a mathematics, not as an engineering discipline; a reviewer could reasonably move it to Applied Engineering Domains.

run2.scope_in: Learning that embeds or replaces a numerical simulation: physics-informed networks, operator and PDE learning, surrogate models, differentiable simulation.
run2.scope_out: The science the simulation is of -> Physical Sciences or Environmental Sciences; statistical inference from simulator outputs -> Probabilistic Inference.
run2.example_children: Physics-Informed Neural Networks; Neural Operators; Partial Differential Equation Solvers
run2.notes: ~25 paper-mentions. Small but methodologically distinct and it gives a clear home to a tail that would otherwise scatter across four branches.

run2.scope_in: Research on properties a deployed model must have beyond accuracy: fairness, transparency, privacy, robustness, calibration, safety, and the norms governing its use.
run2.scope_out: Accuracy on a benchmark -> Evaluation Methodology; making a model smaller -> Model Compression; detecting anomalies as the task -> Anomaly Detection.
run2.example_children: Fairness in Machine Learning; Model Interpretability; Adversarial Robustness
run2.notes: ~200 paper-mentions and the most internally differentiated non-domain branch in this corpus; nine children is justified because each is its own literature with its own venues.

run2.scope_in: Measuring and mitigating disparate model behaviour across groups or individuals.
run2.scope_out: Dataset-level imbalance treated as a label problem -> Supervised Learning; normative and legal argument about AI -> Responsible AI.
run2.example_children: Algorithmic Fairness; Bias Mitigation; Intersectional Fairness
run2.notes: 19 + 12 papers plus ~25 tail names, many of them near-duplicate phrasings ('Fairness in AI', 'Machine Learning Fairness', 'Fairness and Bias'). A strong institute signal.

run2.scope_in: Explaining what a model computes or why it produced an output: attribution, concept-based and mechanistic analysis, surrogate explanations.
run2.scope_out: Inherently simple statistical models used in an applied field -> that field; verifying a formal property -> Neural Network Verification.
run2.example_children: Explainable AI; Mechanistic Interpretability; Feature Importance
run2.notes: ~45 paper-mentions spread over a dozen synonyms (XAI, Explainability, Interpretable Machine Learning, Model Understanding).

run2.scope_in: Protecting the data a model was trained on: differential privacy, inference and reconstruction attacks, unlearning, privacy-preserving computation.
run2.scope_out: Not pooling data across sites as a training architecture -> Federated Learning; data governance policy -> Responsible AI.
run2.example_children: Differential Privacy; Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs); Machine Unlearning
run2.notes: ~25 paper-mentions.

run2.scope_in: Behaviour of models under deliberately crafted inputs or poisoned training data, and defences against them.
run2.scope_out: Degradation under naturally occurring shift -> Distribution-Shift Robustness; flagging outliers as the task -> Anomaly Detection.
run2.example_children: Adversarial Attacks; Adversarial Training; Certified Robustness
run2.notes: 13 + 9 papers plus ~25 tail names, including attacks on language models and model stealing.

run2.scope_in: Keeping performance when test data differs from training data through no adversary: covariate, label and subpopulation shift, worst-group performance, spurious correlation.
run2.scope_out: Adapting to a known target domain with target data -> Transfer Learning; detecting that a sample is out of distribution -> Anomaly Detection.
run2.example_children: Out-of-Distribution Generalization; Covariate Shift; Worst-Group Generalization
run2.notes: ~35 paper-mentions. The scope_out against Anomaly Detection has to be read by any annotator handling an 'OOD' name; the two names differ by one word and mean different literatures.

run2.scope_in: Producing and validating a model's own statement of confidence: calibration, predictive intervals, conformal methods, ensembles as uncertainty estimators.
run2.scope_out: Posterior computation as mathematics -> Probabilistic Inference; measurement uncertainty in a scientific instrument -> that science.
run2.example_children: Uncertainty Estimation; Model Calibration; Conformal Prediction

run2.scope_in: Acquisition, reconstruction, segmentation and analysis of images of the body or of biological specimens.

run2.scope_in: Computational analysis and modelling of biological molecules and systems: sequences, structures, expression, omics, networks.

run2.example_children: Bioinformatics; Genomics; Protein Structure Prediction

run2.scope_in: Biology whose subject is an organism, tissue, cell or immune system rather than a computation over biological data.

run2.example_children: Immunology; Virology; Structural Biology

run2.scope_in: Finding and designing therapeutic molecules: property prediction, generation, synthesis planning, binding, repurposing, response prediction.

run2.notes: ~30 paper-mentions. Separated from Computational Chemistry because its objective is therapeutic, which is how the quotes read.

run2.scope_in: Health at population scale: epidemiology, surveillance, outbreak modelling, health policy, global and environmental health.

run2.example_children: Epidemiology; Global Health; Public Health Surveillance
run2.notes: 20 + 12 + 5 papers plus a COVID-era tail.

run2.example_children: Digital Health; Clinical Decision Support Systems; Telemedicine
run2.notes: ~60 paper-mentions. Also the home for the generic 'AI in healthcare' family ('Healthcare AI', 'Machine Learning for Healthcare', 'AI for Health'), which is large and otherwise homeless.

run2.scope_in: Research whose subject is non-living matter and energy: astrophysics, fundamental physics, chemistry, materials.
run2.scope_out: Climate, ecosystems and the earth surface -> Environmental Sciences; physics-informed learning as a method -> Scientific Machine Learning; medical radiation physics -> Medical Physics.
run2.example_children: Astrophysics; Computational Chemistry; Materials Science
run2.notes: ~110 paper-mentions. Split from Environmental Sciences deliberately: the two share no methods, no data and no collaborators in this corpus.

run2.scope_in: Astronomical and cosmological objects and surveys: galaxies, black holes, gravitational lensing, telescope and radio data.
run2.scope_out: Neutrino and collider experiments -> Fundamental Physics; satellite imagery of Earth -> Environmental Monitoring.
run2.example_children: Cosmology; Galaxy Evolution; Observational Astrophysics
run2.notes: 15 + 5 + 4 papers plus ~15 tail names including astroinformatics and telescope data analysis.

run2.scope_in: Particle, nuclear, high-energy and quantum physics as research subjects, including detector and simulation work.

run2.notes: ~25 paper-mentions. Includes the bare name 'Physics' (5) and quantum mechanics/simulation names.

run2.scope_in: Molecular and atomic systems modelled from chemistry: quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, reaction and catalyst modelling, cheminformatics.

run2.example_children: Quantum Chemistry; Molecular Dynamics; Catalysis
run2.notes: 12 + 4 papers plus ~20 tail names. The seam with Drug Discovery is intent, not method, and some names ('Molecular Design') could go either way.

run2.notes: ~20 paper-mentions spread over 'Material Science', 'Materials Science', 'Materials Modeling', 'Materials Science and Engineering'.

run2.scope_in: Research whose subject is the climate, ecosystems, land surface or agricultural systems.

run2.example_children: Climate Science; Ecology; Environmental Monitoring
run2.notes: ~80 paper-mentions. Small relative to Biomedical Sciences and that asymmetry is real; it is not to be corrected.

run2.scope_in: The climate system and its projection: emulation of climate models, downscaling, impact assessment, emissions accounting.
run2.scope_out: Ecosystem and species response -> Ecology; grid decarbonisation technology -> Energy Systems.
run2.example_children: Climate Model Emulation; Climate Data Downscaling; Climate Change Impact
run2.notes: ~20 paper-mentions.

run2.scope_in: Organisms, populations and ecosystems: biodiversity, species distributions, conservation, animal behaviour, evolutionary and plant biology.

run2.example_children: Biodiversity Monitoring; Species Distribution Modeling; Conservation Biology
run2.notes: ~35 paper-mentions including bioacoustics, trophic and statistical ecology.

run2.scope_in: Observing the earth surface and environment with instruments: remote sensing, aerial and satellite imagery, pollution, fire, seismic and forest monitoring.

run2.notes: 11 + 4 papers plus a tail. Added during the tail check: 'Air Pollution', 'Fire Monitoring' and 'Earthquake Monitoring' had no home under a narrower 'Remote Sensing' name.

run2.example_children: Agricultural Data Analysis; Agriculture and Land Use; Plant Science
run2.notes: Very small (~6 paper-mentions) and retained only because those names genuinely have nowhere else to go. A reviewer may prefer to fold it into Ecology.

run2.scope_in: Research whose subject is a designed artefact or engineered system: robots, software, networks, power systems, vehicles, hardware, industrial operations.

run2.example_children: Robotics; Software Engineering; Energy Systems
run2.notes: ~200 paper-mentions, dominated by software engineering (36) and robotics (25).

run2.scope_in: Embodied agents acting in the physical world: manipulation, locomotion, navigation, SLAM, autonomous vehicles, human-robot interaction, sim-to-real.

run2.example_children: Robotic Manipulation; Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM); Autonomous Driving

run2.scope_in: Building, testing, maintaining and analysing software, including machine learning applied to source code and the engineering of ML-containing systems.

run2.notes: ~30 paper-mentions.

run2.scope_in: Generation, storage, distribution and consumption of energy: grids, demand response, building energy, renewables, carbon capture.

run2.notes: ~30 paper-mentions including a clear building-energy sub-cluster.

run2.scope_in: Movement of people and goods as a domain: transit networks, traffic control, fleet and crew operations, mobility services.

run2.scope_in: Design and synthesis of computing hardware as the research subject, including neuromorphic and quantum computing devices.

run2.notes: ~12 paper-mentions. Thin but the names are unmistakable and belong nowhere else.

run2.example_children: Operations Management; Manufacturing; Production Control
run2.notes: ~12 paper-mentions. The weakest category in this branch; retained because the alternative is putting 'Industry 4.0' and 'Revenue Management' in the residual bucket.

run2.scope_in: Research whose subject is people, their minds, their institutions and their interaction with computing systems.

run2.example_children: Human-Computer Interaction; Cognitive Science; Educational Technology

run2.scope_in: Mind and cognition modelled or measured behaviourally: cognitive architectures, theory of mind, reasoning and memory as psychological phenomena.

run2.notes: ~25 paper-mentions. The seam with Neuroscience is whether the study measures the brain.

run2.scope_in: Behaviour, personality, affect and wellbeing studied as psychological subjects.
run2.scope_out: Psychiatric diagnosis or treatment -> Clinical Medicine; cognitive mechanism modelling -> Cognitive Science.
run2.example_children: Social Psychology; Health Psychology; Behavioral Sciences

run2.scope_in: Markets, incentives, finance and economic behaviour as research subjects.

run2.notes: ~12 paper-mentions. The scope_out against 'Curriculum Learning' matters: that name is a training schedule, not education.

run2.scope_in: Language as an object of linguistic inquiry: syntax, semantics, pragmatics, sociolinguistics, language emergence.
run2.scope_out: Engineering a system that processes text -> Natural Language Processing.
run2.example_children: Computational Linguistics; Sociolinguistics; Syntax
run2.notes: ~15 paper-mentions. Almost every annotator will be tempted to send these to NLP; the distinction is whether the claim is about language or about a system.
