run2.notes: ~12 paper-mentions. Overlaps Responsible AI by subject matter; the split is whether AI is the thing being governed.

run3.scope_in: Names for the structure of the training signal and of the data stream a learner is given, independent of data type or application.
run3.scope_out: Not the data type (text, graphs) -> Modality-Specific Machine Learning; not the agent-over-time setting -> Sequential Decision Making; bare 'Machine Learning' / 'Deep Learning' -> Non-Specific Research Labels.
run3.example_children: Self-Supervised Learning; Transfer Learning; Continual Learning
run3.notes: Nine children because the corpus names nine distinct supervision regimes, each with its own literature; the sizes are very unequal (SSL ~100 mentions, Multi-Task ~25) and that is the intended measurement.

run3.scope_in: Learning a mapping from fully labelled examples, including work on label noise, class imbalance and cost structure.
run3.scope_out: Semi-supervised, few-shot or active label acquisition -> Learning with Limited Supervision; bare 'Classification'/'Regression' used as a field label rather than a studied problem -> Non-Specific Research Labels.
run3.example_children: Learning with Noisy Labels; Imbalanced Classification; Cost-sensitive Learning
run3.notes: Small (~25 mentions). Most supervised work in this corpus is named by its modality instead, which is itself a finding.

run3.scope_in: Learning when labels are scarce, partial, or must be acquired: semi-supervised, weakly supervised, few-shot, zero-shot and active learning.
run3.scope_out: Learning with no labels at all -> Unsupervised Learning; labels invented from the data itself -> Self-Supervised Learning; reusing a model from another task -> Transfer Learning.
run3.example_children: Semi-Supervised Learning; Few-Shot Learning; Active Learning
run3.notes: Zero-Shot Learning sits here rather than under Transfer Learning because in this corpus it is named as a label-scarcity setting, not as a domain-shift setting.

run3.scope_in: Learning structure from unlabelled data without a constructed pretext task: clustering, density-based grouping, unsupervised discovery.
run3.scope_out: Pretext-task training -> Self-Supervised Learning; learning an embedding geometry -> Representation Learning; fitting a sampler -> Deep Generative Modelling.
run3.example_children: Clustering; Unsupervised Object Discovery; Unsupervised Representation Learning
run3.notes: Boundary with Representation Learning is the weakest in this branch; the deciding question is whether the name emphasises the absence of labels or the properties of the learned code.

run3.scope_in: Training on labels constructed from the input itself: contrastive, masked-prediction and other pretext objectives, and large-scale pre-training framed that way.
run3.scope_out: The properties of the resulting embedding (disentanglement, invariance) -> Representation Learning; adapting a pre-trained model to a task -> Transfer Learning.
run3.example_children: Contrastive Learning; Self-Supervised Learning (SSL); Pre-Training Techniques
run3.notes: ~100 mentions and growing fast in the corpus; the paired Representation Learning node measures the other half of the same programme.

run3.scope_in: Reusing a model or representation trained on one distribution or task on another, including fine-tuning, domain adaptation with target data, and in-context adaptation.
run3.scope_out: Generalising to an unseen distribution with no target data -> Distribution Shift Robustness; learning an adaptation procedure itself -> Meta-Learning; cheap-parameter variants of fine-tuning -> Parameter-Efficient Adaptation.
run3.example_children: Domain Adaptation; Sim-to-Real Transfer; In-Context Learning
run3.notes: The Domain Adaptation / Domain Generalization split (target data available or not) is a real distinction in the corpus and annotators must be held to it.

run3.scope_in: Learning the learning procedure itself: learned initialisations, learned optimisers, learned adaptation rules.
run3.scope_out: Simply evaluating on few labels -> Learning with Limited Supervision; tuning hyperparameters with a search method -> Black-Box Optimization.
run3.example_children: Meta-Reinforcement Learning; Meta-gradient Learning; Hyperparameter Generalization
run3.notes: Borderline under rule 3: 'Meta-Learning' itself is 26 papers but its distinct children are thin. Kept because merging it into Transfer Learning would hide a named community.

run3.scope_in: Learning from a non-stationary or sequentially arriving data stream, including forgetting, plasticity loss, and online/incremental/lifelong variants.
run3.scope_out: Many tasks presented simultaneously -> Multi-Task Learning; a shift between a fixed train and test distribution -> Distribution Shift Robustness.
run3.example_children: Catastrophic Forgetting; Lifelong Learning; Online Continual Learning
run3.notes: Deliberately absorbs 'Online Learning', 'Incremental Learning' and 'Sequential Learning'; bandit-style online decision names go to Reinforcement Learning instead.

run3.scope_in: Training across clients that do not pool their data, and the aggregation, heterogeneity and communication problems that creates.
run3.scope_out: Multi-machine training of one model on one dataset -> Distributed Training; the privacy guarantee itself -> Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning.
run3.example_children: Decentralized Learning; Model Aggregation; Communication-Efficient Learning
run3.notes: Sits in paradigms, not systems, because the corpus names it for the data-locality constraint, not for throughput.

run3.scope_in: Training one model on several tasks or objectives at once, and the interference and weighting problems that follow.
run3.scope_out: Tasks presented in sequence -> Continual Learning; auxiliary objectives used only to shape an RL agent -> Reinforcement Learning.
run3.example_children: Multi-Objective Learning; Multi-task Reinforcement Learning; Auxiliary Tasks
run3.notes: Small (~25) but conceptually distinct from both transfer and continual learning.

run3.scope_in: Names for computing or learning a policy for an agent that acts over time under uncertainty, including the formalisms and the control-theoretic side.
run3.scope_out: Static prediction from a fixed dataset -> Learning Paradigms; the optimisation algorithm used inside a solver -> Mathematical Optimization; the robot hardware or task -> Robotics.
run3.example_children: Reinforcement Learning; Control Theory; Imitation Learning
run3.notes: The largest single coherent methodological family in the corpus after modality work (~500 mentions). Bandit names are placed here, not under online learning, because the corpus frames them as exploration problems.

run3.scope_in: Learning a policy from reward, including deep RL, offline/online RL, exploration, credit assignment, value estimation and bandit formulations.
run3.scope_out: Learning from demonstrations or preferences rather than reward -> Imitation Learning; several interacting learners -> Multi-Agent Learning; model-based planning in a known MDP -> Planning under Uncertainty.
run3.example_children: Deep Reinforcement Learning; Offline Reinforcement Learning; Policy Gradient Methods
run3.notes: ~400 mentions, the second-largest depth-2 node. Safe/robust/risk-averse RL stay here (constraint inside the objective) rather than moving to Trustworthy Machine Learning.

run3.scope_in: Analysis and synthesis of controllers for dynamical systems: stability, optimal control, model-predictive and networked control, system identification.
run3.scope_out: Reward-driven policy learning -> Reinforcement Learning; robot-specific tasks and hardware -> Robotics; grid or traffic operation -> Infrastructure Systems.
run3.example_children: Optimal Control; Model Predictive Control; Lyapunov Stability
run3.notes: 'Continuous Control' is ambiguous; route it here only when the name is about the control formulation, otherwise to Reinforcement Learning.

run3.scope_in: Decision-process formalisms and search over them: MDPs, POMDPs, dynamic programming, probabilistic and symbolic planning.
run3.scope_out: Learning the policy from experience -> Reinforcement Learning; motion planning for a physical robot -> Robotics.
run3.example_children: Markov Decision Processes; Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes; Probabilistic Planning
run3.notes: Small (~20) but needed: these names describe the formalism, not the learning algorithm, and merging them into RL would misattribute theory work.

run3.scope_in: Settings with several interacting decision makers, including game-theoretic equilibria, cooperation, coordination and emergent communication.
run3.scope_out: A single agent in a stochastic environment -> Reinforcement Learning; multi-robot hardware coordination -> Robotics; social-welfare policy questions -> Social Sciences.
run3.example_children: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning; Game Theory; Multi-Agent Systems
run3.notes: 'Game Theory' (20 papers) lands here rather than in a mathematics branch because its corpus context is learning in games.

run3.scope_in: Learning behaviour from demonstrations, preferences or human feedback rather than from an environment reward.
run3.scope_out: Reward-driven learning -> Reinforcement Learning; the alignment objective as a safety question -> AI Safety.
run3.example_children: Inverse Reinforcement Learning; Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback; Reward Learning
run3.notes: Separated from RL because the supervision source is different and the corpus names it separately ~25 times.

run3.scope_in: Names for modelling a distribution over data or latent quantities and for inferring from it, including generative model families and causal structure.
run3.scope_out: Modelling a specific data type -> Modality-Specific Machine Learning; the architecture used to parameterise the model -> Neural Architecture Design; calibration of a discriminative model -> Uncertainty Quantification.
run3.example_children: Generative Models; Bayesian Inference; Causal Inference
run3.notes: Three children only; density estimation, latent-variable and Monte Carlo names are absorbed rather than split out because they do not reach three distinct children each.

run3.scope_in: Learning to sample from a data distribution with a neural model, and the model families used to do it.
run3.scope_out: Generating text -> Natural Language Processing; generating images or video -> Computer Vision; the network wiring studied for its own sake -> Neural Architecture Design.
run3.example_children: Diffusion Models; Normalizing Flows; Generative Adversarial Networks
run3.notes: ~180 mentions. The largest concentration of architecture-shaped names in the corpus; they are placed by the problem they solve, per the architecture policy.

run3.scope_in: Bayesian modelling and posterior inference: variational methods, Monte Carlo, simulation-based inference, Gaussian processes, graphical models.
run3.scope_out: Point-estimate uncertainty heuristics on a trained net -> Uncertainty Quantification; optimisation of an acquisition function for experiment design -> Black-Box Optimization.
run3.example_children: Variational Inference; Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC); Simulation-Based Inference
run3.notes: Deliberately wide: it holds both the modelling and the inference-algorithm names, which annotators cannot reliably separate.

run3.scope_in: Reasoning about interventions and causal structure: discovery, identifiability, treatment-effect estimation, causal representations.
run3.scope_out: Correlational prediction in an applied field -> the applied domain; disentanglement judged only by representation quality -> Representation Learning.
run3.example_children: Causal Discovery; Causal Representation Learning; Identifiability Theory
run3.notes: ~45 mentions. Placed under probabilistic modelling rather than at top level because every name here is about inferring a distribution under intervention.

run3.scope_in: Names whose object is the neural network itself: how it is wired, what it encodes, how it is trained and why it generalises.
run3.scope_out: Bare 'Deep Learning' / 'Neural Networks' as a field label -> Non-Specific Research Labels; making a network cheaper -> Computational Efficiency in Machine Learning; proving bounds -> Learning Theory.
run3.example_children: Representation Learning; Neural Network Architectures; Neural Network Training
run3.notes: This node exists so that architecture names have a principled home without becoming an axis of their own; see the architecture policy in RATIONALE.md.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is the structure of a network: attention, recurrence, convolution, equivariance, modularity, architecture search.
run3.scope_out: Architecture families defined by the input structure (graph networks) -> Graph Machine Learning; generative model families -> Deep Generative Modelling; compression of an architecture -> Model Compression.
run3.example_children: Transformers; Attention Mechanisms; Neural Architecture Search
run3.notes: ~95 paper-mentions (1.6%) land here. This is the node that overlaps the separate model-architecture ontology and it is isolated so the survey can subtract or cross-check it.

run3.scope_in: What a model encodes and the geometry of that code: disentanglement, invariance, embeddings, metric and manifold structure, object-centric codes.
run3.scope_out: The training objective that produced it -> Self-Supervised Learning; a domain-specific embedding (molecules, proteins) -> the applied domain; reducing dimension purely to compress -> Model Compression.
run3.example_children: Disentanglement; Manifold Learning; Object-Centric Learning
run3.notes: ~120 mentions. Kept distinct from Self-Supervised Learning: SSL is how you train, Representation Learning is what you then claim about the code.

run3.scope_in: Empirical study of how networks are fitted: gradient methods in practice, training dynamics, initialisation, normalisation, regularisation, loss design.
run3.scope_out: Optimisation studied for convergence guarantees -> Continuous Optimization; multi-machine throughput -> Distributed Training; hyperparameter search -> Black-Box Optimization.
run3.example_children: Stochastic Gradient Descent; Training Dynamics; Sharpness-Aware Minimization
run3.notes: The line against Continuous Optimization is empirical-vs-proof; it is stated so annotators do not route every 'Optimization' name into mathematics.

run3.scope_in: Empirical study of why and when trained networks generalise: scaling behaviour, memorisation, implicit bias, compositional and systematic generalisation.
run3.scope_out: Proved generalisation bounds -> Statistical Learning Theory; generalisation across a distribution shift -> Distribution Shift Robustness.
run3.example_children: Scaling Laws; Implicit Regularization; Systematic Generalization
run3.notes: Small (~25) and overlaps Learning Theory; kept separate because the corpus's names here are measured, not proved.

run3.scope_in: Names for bodies of research organised around a kind of data - text, images, audio, graphs, time series, several at once - including the tasks native to that data.
run3.scope_out: A field of application that happens to use images or text (medical imaging, remote sensing) -> Applied Research Domains; a learning paradigm demonstrated on one modality -> Learning Paradigms.
run3.example_children: Natural Language Processing; Computer Vision; Graph Machine Learning
run3.notes: The single largest family (~1300 mentions). A parent is used rather than six top-level nodes because these communities share one organising principle, and the survey wants the modality-specific versus modality-agnostic ratio.

run3.scope_in: Learning over text and language: language modelling, translation, generation, parsing, question answering, multilinguality, and language-model behaviour.
run3.scope_out: Linguistics as a scientific field -> Social Sciences; code as the text -> Software Engineering; text paired with images -> Multimodal Learning; evaluation methodology for NLG -> Evaluation Metrics.
run3.example_children: Machine Translation; Question Answering; Language Modeling
run3.notes: The largest depth-2 node (~550 mentions). Large-language-model names (prompting, instruction tuning, RAG, in-context learning) land here unless they name a trust property.

run3.scope_in: Learning over images, video and 3D visual data, including recognition, segmentation, reconstruction, neural rendering and visual generation.
run3.scope_out: Medical or satellite images as a field of study -> Applied Research Domains; images paired with text -> Multimodal Learning; the generative model family itself -> Deep Generative Modelling.
run3.example_children: Image Classification; Object Detection; Semantic Segmentation
run3.notes: Absorbs computer graphics and neural rendering (~25 mentions) rather than giving them a sibling node; flagged as an uncertain call.

run3.scope_in: Learning over acoustic signals: speech recognition and synthesis, speaker modelling, music, environmental and bioacoustic sound.
run3.scope_out: Language content independent of the signal -> Natural Language Processing; clinical biosignals (EEG, ECG) -> Neuroscience or Health Research.
run3.example_children: Speech Recognition; Speech Synthesis; Music Information Retrieval (MIR)
run3.notes: ~45 mentions. Named 'Audio' rather than 'Speech' so music and bioacoustics are not orphaned.

run3.scope_in: Learning over graph-structured data: message passing, node and edge prediction, graph generation, expressivity, dynamic and heterophilic graphs.
run3.scope_out: Molecular graphs studied to predict chemistry -> Physical Sciences; social network content analysis -> Social Sciences; graph algorithms as combinatorics -> Combinatorial Optimization.
run3.example_children: Graph Neural Networks; Node Classification; Link Prediction
run3.notes: ~200 mentions. 'Graph Neural Networks' (76 papers) is treated as naming this research area, not an architecture, on the evidence of its corpus context.

run3.scope_in: Learning over ordered numeric sequences: forecasting, temporal representation, change-point and temporal anomaly structure, point processes.
run3.scope_out: Text or audio sequences -> their own modality; a clinical or energy forecasting application -> the applied domain; RL trajectories -> Reinforcement Learning.
run3.example_children: Time Series Forecasting; Time Series Analysis; Temporal Point Processes
run3.notes: ~40 mentions. Smaller than one would expect from the applied names, because forecasting work is usually named by its domain.

run3.scope_in: Learning that binds two or more modalities in one model: vision-language, audio-text, cross-modal alignment and retrieval.
run3.scope_out: A single modality -> its own node; generation conditioned on text but evaluated purely as imagery -> Computer Vision.
run3.example_children: Vision-Language Models; Visual Question Answering; Cross-Modal Learning
run3.notes: ~50 mentions and rising; kept separate because the research question is alignment, not either modality.

run3.scope_in: Names for optimisation problems and algorithms studied for their formulation and guarantees, including discrete and operational decision problems.
run3.scope_out: Empirical tuning of neural network training -> Neural Network Training; learning a policy over time -> Sequential Decision Making; optimisation of a physical plant -> Infrastructure Systems.
run3.example_children: Convex Optimization; Combinatorial Optimization; Bayesian Optimization
run3.notes: Bare 'Optimization' (71 papers) rests at this parent and must not be pushed to a child; that is a real ~1.2% mass of unresolvable names.

run3.scope_in: Optimisation over continuous variables with a guarantee focus: convex and non-convex analysis, stochastic and first-order methods, minimax and variational inequalities.
run3.scope_out: Measured behaviour of SGD on real networks -> Neural Network Training; derivative-free search -> Black-Box Optimization.
run3.example_children: Convex Optimization; Stochastic Optimization; First-Order Methods
run3.notes: ~90 mentions; a distinct and visible group in this corpus.

run3.scope_in: Discrete and operational decision problems and their solvers: integer programming, routing, scheduling, constraint and SAT solving, learning-to-optimise for them.
run3.scope_out: Graph representation learning -> Graph Machine Learning; continuous relaxations studied for convergence -> Continuous Optimization.
run3.example_children: Mixed Integer Programming; Vehicle Routing Problem; Operations Research
run3.notes: Deliberately absorbs Operations Research (19 papers) and its problem names; splitting OR from combinatorics produced two nodes annotators could not separate.

run3.scope_in: Optimising an expensive or unknown objective by querying it: Bayesian optimisation, surrogates, evolutionary search, hyperparameter search, AutoML.
run3.scope_out: Gradient-based training -> Neural Network Training; designing molecules where the science is the point -> Physical Sciences or Life Sciences.
run3.example_children: Bayesian Optimization; Hyper-Parameter Optimization; Evolutionary Algorithms
run3.notes: ~35 mentions; distinct because the defining constraint is query access, not convexity.

run3.scope_in: Names for proved statements about learning: generalisation, sample complexity, expressivity, convergence, and theory-of-computation names used as topics.
run3.scope_out: Measured generalisation of real networks -> Generalization in Deep Learning; optimisation algorithm design -> Mathematical Optimization.
run3.example_children: Statistical Learning Theory; Theory of Deep Learning; Generalization Bounds
run3.notes: Only two children; theory-of-computation names (Theoretical Computer Science, Automata Theory) rest at this parent. ~55 mentions, small on purpose.

run3.scope_in: Bounds and complexity results for learning: generalisation bounds, sample complexity, PAC-Bayes, risk minimisation, high-dimensional statistics.
run3.scope_out: Empirical scaling curves -> Generalization in Deep Learning; information-theoretic coding for communication -> Infrastructure Systems.
run3.example_children: Generalization Bounds; Sample Complexity; PAC-Bayesian Theory
run3.notes: Information-theoretic names used as learning theory (information bottleneck, entropy regularisation) are placed here.

run3.scope_in: Mathematical analysis of neural networks specifically: kernel limits, expressivity, loss-landscape geometry, random-matrix and convergence analysis.
run3.scope_out: Experiments on training behaviour -> Neural Network Training; architecture proposals -> Neural Architecture Design.
run3.example_children: Neural Tangent Kernel; Loss Landscape Analysis; Mathematics of Deep Learning
run3.notes: Overlaps Generalization in Deep Learning; the test is whether the claim is proved or measured.

run3.scope_in: Names for properties of a trained system audited from outside the objective: fairness, privacy, interpretability, robustness, uncertainty, safety and governance.
run3.scope_out: A constraint written into a decision objective (safe or risk-averse RL) -> Sequential Decision Making; ethics of a profession rather than of an ML system (medical ethics) -> Applied Research Domains; accuracy benchmarking -> Evaluation Metrics.
run3.example_children: Fairness in Machine Learning; Adversarial Robustness; Model Interpretability
run3.notes: ~370 mentions. Nine children because each is a separate community with its own venues; this is where rule 6 is knowingly exceeded.

run3.scope_in: Measuring and mitigating disparate model behaviour across groups or individuals.
run3.scope_out: Fairness of a health system independent of a model -> Health Research; representational bias in a dataset studied as data quality -> Data Quality.
run3.example_children: Algorithmic Fairness; Bias Mitigation; Intersectional Fairness
run3.notes: ~55 mentions across many near-duplicate names ('Fairness in AI', 'Machine Learning Fairness', 'Fairness and Bias'); normalising them is most of the work here.

run3.scope_in: Protecting training data from disclosure by the model: differential privacy, inference and reconstruction attacks, unlearning.
run3.scope_out: Training without pooling data as a learning setting -> Federated Learning; data governance policy -> AI Governance.
run3.example_children: Differential Privacy; Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs); Machine Unlearning
run3.notes: ~30 mentions. Overlaps Federated Learning; the test is whether the name asserts a privacy property or a training topology.

run3.scope_in: Explaining what a model computed or why: post-hoc attribution, concept-based explanation, mechanistic analysis of internals.
run3.scope_out: Visualising data rather than a model -> Empirical Methodology; probing a language model for linguistic structure -> Natural Language Processing.
run3.example_children: Explainable AI; Mechanistic Interpretability; Feature Importance
run3.notes: ~65 mentions under at least eight surface spellings of 'explainable AI'.

run3.scope_in: Behaviour under adversarially chosen inputs or training data, and certification against it.
run3.scope_out: Naturally occurring shift -> Distribution Shift Robustness; detecting anomalous but non-adversarial inputs -> Anomaly Detection.
run3.example_children: Adversarial Attacks; Adversarial Training; Certified Robustness
run3.notes: Neural Network Verification is placed here rather than under theory, because its corpus use is certification of robustness.

run3.scope_in: Maintaining performance on distributions unseen at training time, without access to target data.
run3.scope_out: Adaptation using target data -> Transfer Learning; adversarially crafted shift -> Adversarial Robustness.
run3.example_children: Out-of-Distribution Generalization; Domain Generalization; Worst-Group Generalization
run3.notes: ~35 mentions. The Domain Generalization / Domain Adaptation boundary is the single most error-prone call in this structure.

run3.scope_in: Knowing how much to trust a prediction: calibration, predictive intervals, conformal methods, out-of-distribution detection.
run3.scope_out: Full posterior modelling -> Bayesian Inference; detecting rare events as a task -> Anomaly Detection.
run3.example_children: Model Calibration; Conformal Prediction; Out-of-Distribution Detection
run3.notes: ~40 mentions. Split from Bayesian Inference deliberately: these names are about auditing a fixed model, not about a probabilistic model class.

run3.scope_in: Identifying inputs that deviate from learned normal behaviour, in any modality, including fraud, faults and log anomalies.
run3.scope_out: Distribution shift of the whole test set -> Distribution Shift Robustness; supervised rare-class prediction -> Supervised Learning.
run3.example_children: Outlier Detection; Time-Series Anomaly Detection; Graph Anomaly Detection (GAD)
run3.notes: ~30 mentions. The least comfortable placement in this proposal: many of these names are plain tasks, not trust properties.

run3.scope_in: Preventing harmful or unintended model behaviour at the level of goals and capabilities: alignment, misuse, risk, goal misgeneralisation.
run3.scope_out: Constrained decision-making formalisms -> Sequential Decision Making; regulation and policy -> AI Governance.
run3.example_children: AI Alignment; AI Risk; Goal Misgeneralization
run3.notes: ~20 mentions; small but named explicitly and repeatedly enough to be real.

run3.scope_in: Ethics, policy, regulation and accountability frameworks for deployed AI systems.
run3.scope_out: Ethics of a clinical or scientific practice -> the applied domain; a technical fairness metric -> Fairness in Machine Learning.
run3.example_children: AI Ethics; AI Regulation; Responsible AI
run3.notes: ~55 mentions in a very large number of one-paper spellings ('Ethics of AI', 'Ethical AI', 'AI Ethics and Society'); normalisation matters more here than anywhere else.

run3.scope_in: Names whose object is the compute, memory, energy or communication cost of building or running a model.
run3.scope_out: Algorithmic convergence rates -> Mathematical Optimization; training across data silos -> Federated Learning; hardware as an engineering field -> Infrastructure Systems.
run3.example_children: Model Compression; Distributed Training; Hardware Acceleration
run3.notes: Named for cost rather than 'ML Systems' so it does not attract 'Multi-Agent Systems', 'Recommender Systems' or 'Control Systems'. ~110 mentions.

run3.scope_in: Making a trained model smaller or sparser: pruning, quantisation, distillation, low-rank and sparse structure.
run3.scope_out: Efficient adaptation of a frozen model -> Parameter-Efficient Adaptation; architecture search for efficiency -> Neural Architecture Design.
run3.example_children: Knowledge Distillation; Model Pruning; Quantization
run3.notes: ~45 mentions and the most self-consistent naming in this branch.

run3.scope_in: Running one training job across many devices: data and model parallelism, communication cost, large-scale infrastructure.
run3.scope_out: Clients withholding data -> Federated Learning; parallel algorithms studied for convergence -> Continuous Optimization.
run3.example_children: Model Parallelism; Distributed Deep Learning; Communication Efficiency
run3.notes: ~25 mentions.

run3.scope_in: Executing models on specific hardware, and compilers and circuits designed for them.
run3.scope_out: Chip design as an engineering discipline -> Infrastructure Systems; neuromorphic models used to study the brain -> Neuroscience.
run3.example_children: Neuromorphic Computing; Deep Learning Compilers; FPGA Synthesis
run3.notes: ~25 mentions; the smallest child here and the one whose boundary with electrical engineering is softest.

run3.scope_in: Adapting a large pre-trained model by training few parameters.
run3.scope_out: Full fine-tuning or domain adaptation -> Transfer Learning; compressing the base model -> Model Compression.
run3.example_children: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT); Parameter-efficient Learning; Parameter-Efficient Training
run3.notes: Only ~5 mentions but three distinct names; kept because it is the one efficiency concept the corpus names in its own right rather than as compression.

run3.scope_in: Names whose object is the apparatus of ML research rather than a model: how datasets are built and cleaned and how results are measured.
run3.scope_out: A dataset built for a specific science -> the applied domain; measuring a trust property -> Trustworthy Machine Learning; the learning setting -> Learning Paradigms.
run3.example_children: Benchmarking; Evaluation Metrics; Dataset Creation
run3.notes: ~120 mentions. This is one node rather than two ('data' and 'evaluation') because benchmark work in this corpus routinely spans both.

run3.scope_in: Designing, running and reporting benchmark comparisons, including reproducibility and open-science practice around them.
run3.scope_out: Proposing a metric -> Evaluation Metrics; building the dataset itself -> Dataset Construction.
run3.example_children: Benchmark Design; NLP Benchmarking; Empirical Benchmarking
run3.notes: Reproducibility and open-science names rest here; they are too few to support their own node.

run3.scope_in: Proposing, analysing or criticising the measures used to score models.
run3.scope_out: Benchmark suites -> Benchmarking; calibration as a trust property -> Uncertainty Quantification.
run3.example_children: Model Evaluation; Metric Evaluation; Evaluation Metrics for Natural Language Generation
run3.notes: ~35 mentions; strongly represented in the one-paper tail for language and multimodal evaluation.

run3.scope_in: Collecting, curating, annotating and releasing datasets and corpora as the contribution.
run3.scope_out: Cleaning or repairing an existing dataset -> Data Quality; generating training data from a model -> Data Augmentation.
run3.example_children: Dataset Creation; Data Curation; Multilingual Text Corpus Creation
run3.notes: Domain-specific dataset papers (clinical, ecological) go to the applied domain by the precedence rule; this node keeps the methodology papers.

run3.scope_in: Diagnosing and repairing defects in data: noise, missingness, duplication, leakage, valuation and documentation.
run3.scope_out: Learning algorithms designed for noisy labels -> Supervised Learning; fairness audits of a dataset -> Fairness in Machine Learning.
run3.example_children: Data Cleaning in Machine Learning; Data Imputation; Data Valuation
run3.notes: ~20 mentions, almost entirely in the one-paper tail.

run3.scope_in: Enlarging or synthesising training data, and evaluating synthetic data.
run3.scope_out: Generative modelling as the research object -> Deep Generative Modelling; simulation of a physical system -> the applied domain.
run3.example_children: Text Data Augmentation; Synthetic Data; Synthetic Data Evaluation
run3.notes: ~25 mentions. Kept separate from Dataset Construction because the corpus consistently distinguishes collecting data from manufacturing it.

run3.scope_in: Names that denote the field of study, practice or industry the work serves, rather than a machine-learning concept.
run3.scope_out: A learning method that merely borrows a domain word ('Physics-Informed Neural Networks') -> the method category; a data modality studied generically -> Modality-Specific Machine Learning.
run3.example_children: Healthcare; Bioinformatics; Neuroscience
run3.notes: ~1800 mentions (30%). Eleven children, one per field cluster that the corpus actually supports with three or more distinct sub-areas; this is where most of the one-paper tail lives.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is human health, clinical practice, care delivery or the physics and informatics of medicine.
run3.scope_out: Brain science as science rather than care -> Neuroscience; molecular mechanism without a clinical target -> Life Sciences; image-processing methods with no medical subject -> Computer Vision.
run3.example_children: Medical Imaging; Medical Physics; Public Health
run3.notes: The largest applied cluster (~460 mentions) and the widest: it spans clinical specialties, medical imaging, radiation physics, epidemiology and health informatics, which are five real depth-3 nodes.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is biological systems below the level of the organism's clinical care: genomes, proteins, cells, molecules of therapeutic interest, ecology excluded.
run3.scope_out: Human disease management -> Health Research; brains and behaviour -> Neuroscience; ecosystems and species -> Environmental Science.
run3.example_children: Bioinformatics; Genomics; Protein Structure Prediction
run3.notes: ~330 mentions. Drug discovery is placed here rather than in chemistry because its corpus context is therapeutic.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is nervous systems and cognition: neural data, brain imaging, computational models of neural function, brain-machine interfaces.
run3.scope_out: Clinical treatment of neurological disease -> Health Research; neural networks as ML models -> Neural Network Methodology; psychology without neural measurement -> Social Sciences.
run3.example_children: Computational Neuroscience; Neuroimaging; Cognitive Neuroscience
run3.notes: ~250 mentions, large enough to stand beside Health and Life Sciences rather than nest under them, and distinctive of this institute.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is physics, chemistry, materials or astronomy, including simulation of physical and chemical systems.
run3.scope_out: Molecules studied as drugs -> Life Sciences; radiation physics for treatment -> Health Research; physics-inspired ML losses with no physical claim -> Neural Network Methodology.
run3.example_children: Astrophysics; Computational Chemistry; Materials Science
run3.notes: ~120 mentions. Chemistry and physics are one node because the corpus's chemistry names (molecular dynamics, interatomic potentials, quantum chemistry) are physics-of-molecules names.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is the Earth system and living environment: climate, weather, ecology, biodiversity, conservation, land and agriculture.
run3.scope_out: Species genomes -> Life Sciences; satellite sensor processing with no environmental question -> Computer Vision; energy infrastructure -> Infrastructure Systems.
run3.example_children: Climate Science; Ecology; Remote Sensing
run3.notes: ~80 mentions and heavily one-paper: conservation, biodiversity monitoring and downscaling names almost never repeat.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is physical embodied agents: manipulation, locomotion, navigation, SLAM, autonomous vehicles, human-robot interaction.
run3.scope_out: Control formalisms with no robot -> Control Theory; RL algorithms benchmarked in simulation -> Reinforcement Learning; the simulation-to-real gap as a transfer problem -> Transfer Learning.
run3.example_children: Robotic Manipulation; Autonomous Driving; Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM)
run3.notes: ~120 mentions. Placed in applied domains, not methods, so that 'Reinforcement Learning for Robotics' resolves by the domain-first precedence rule.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is software and its construction: code, testing, bugs, maintenance, developer practice, program analysis and synthesis.
run3.scope_out: Language modelling of natural text -> Natural Language Processing; ML pipelines studied for cost -> Computational Efficiency in Machine Learning.
run3.example_children: Software Testing; Code Generation; Program Synthesis
run3.notes: ~110 mentions and a genuinely separate community in this corpus, including empirical SE and ML-for-code.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is people using computing systems: interfaces, usability, accessibility, mixed reality, human factors, sociotechnical deployment.
run3.scope_out: Recommendation algorithms -> Information Retrieval; psychology without an interface -> Social Sciences; governance of AI -> AI Governance.
run3.example_children: Virtual Reality; Accessibility; Human Factors
run3.notes: ~60 mentions. Its one-paper tail (creativity support, gerontechnology, co-design) is large relative to its head.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is matching items to an information need: search, ranking, recommendation, entity matching, personalisation.
run3.scope_out: Question answering over text -> Natural Language Processing; retrieval as a component of a generative pipeline -> Natural Language Processing; graph link prediction -> Graph Machine Learning.
run3.example_children: Recommender Systems; Learning to Rank; Image Retrieval
run3.notes: ~57 mentions. The most debatable placement in this proposal: these are methods papers, but in this corpus they name a product-facing field alongside software engineering and HCI.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is human behaviour, institutions, markets or education, studied as such.
run3.scope_out: Fairness of an ML system -> Fairness in Machine Learning; neural measurement of cognition -> Neuroscience; health policy -> Health Research.
run3.example_children: Cognitive Science; Econometrics; Education
run3.notes: ~80 mentions across economics, psychology, education, linguistics-as-science and policy; each too small alone, and studied together at this institute.

run3.scope_in: Research whose subject is engineered physical networks and plants: telecommunications, electrical power, transportation, buildings, manufacturing.
run3.scope_out: Routing and scheduling as combinatorial problems -> Combinatorial Optimization; control formalisms -> Control Theory; chips for ML -> Hardware Acceleration.
run3.example_children: Telecommunications; Power Systems; Transportation
run3.notes: ~80 mentions. The name is chosen to repel 'Multi-Agent Systems' and 'Decision Support Systems', which a broader 'Engineering' label would attract.

run3.scope_in: Names that identify the field or the activity of research without identifying an area: field-wide umbrellas and generic methodological descriptors.
run3.scope_out: Any name that resolves to a method family, a modality, a trust property or a field -> that category. Only names that would be true of a large fraction of the corpus belong here.
run3.example_children: Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Data Analysis
run3.notes: 523 paper-mentions, 8.7% of the corpus, in 47 names. This is a reported quantity, not a dustbin: it measures how often extraction returned a label with no discriminative content.

run3.scope_in: Names for the discipline as a whole or one of its major named eras.
run3.scope_out: 'Deep Reinforcement Learning' or 'Geometric Deep Learning' -> the specific method family; 'Machine Learning for Chemistry' -> the applied domain.
run3.example_children: Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Artificial Intelligence
run3.notes: 'Machine Learning' (249 papers) and 'Deep Learning' (177) alone are 7% of all paper-mentions - the third and fifth most frequent names in the corpus carry no information.

run3.scope_in: Names for a research activity or posture rather than a subject: analysis, modelling, applications, interdisciplinarity.
run3.scope_out: 'Time Series Analysis' or 'Single-cell Analysis' -> the specific area; 'Empirical Software Engineering' -> Software Engineering.
run3.example_children: Data Analysis; Empirical Study; Interdisciplinary Studies
run3.notes: Includes the extraction's own fallback labels such as 'Interdisciplinary - Other'; keeping them visible lets the survey report extraction quality.
